segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Hello, and welcome back to Imagination Nights. [pause 3]

Settle into the bed. Pull the covers up to where you like them. [pause 8]

Take one deep breath, and let it go with a sigh. [pause 8]

Now let your breathing find its own pace. You do not have to control it. Just notice it. [pause 10]

Feel your feet getting heavy. Your legs. Your back sinking into the mattress. [pause 10]

Now let us relax the body, one part at a time. You do not have to do anything. Just notice each part as I name it, and let it get heavy. [pause 8]

Your feet. Let them be warm and heavy. [pause 15]

Your calves and your knees. Heavy. [pause 15]

Your hips and your lower back. Let them sink. [pause 15]

Your belly. Let it rise and fall on its own. [pause 15]

Your chest. Your shoulders. Your arms, all the way down to your fingertips. [pause 15]

Your neck. Your face. The little muscles around your eyes. [pause 15]

Your whole body, heavy and warm, held by the bed. [pause 15]

The day is finished. This part of the night is yours. [pause 8]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Tonight's wish is not about getting something. It is about how you feel about yourself. [pause 16]

Many of us talk to ourselves at night in ways we would never talk to a friend. We list our mistakes. We call ourselves names. We wonder why we are like this. [pause 18]

Tonight we practice a different voice. We picture a version of you, some months from now, who has made peace with who you are. Not perfect. Just kind to yourself, steady and unashamed. [pause 18]

If the voice in your head has been very hard on you for a long time, or if you have thoughts of hurting yourself, please talk to someone in the daytime. In the United States you can call or text 988 at any hour. You deserve help and you deserve kindness. [pause 18]

This is imagination and feeling, not a promise. But practicing a kind voice is a good way to end the day. [pause 23]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
You are standing in front of a mirror, some months from now. [pause 25]

Look at your own face. Notice that you do not look away. [pause 28]

Notice your eyes. They look rested. [pause 28]

Hear yourself say, in your mind, good morning. And mean it. [pause 28]

Picture yourself making a small mistake later that day. Spilling something. Forgetting a name. [pause 28]

Hear how you speak to yourself now. That is all right. Everybody does that. You laugh a little and move on. [pause 30]

Picture someone giving you a compliment. Notice that you can say thank you without arguing. [pause 30]

In the evening, picture sitting quietly by yourself. It feels like good company. [pause 30]

Say softly, I am enough as I am, and I am still growing. [pause 30]

Let that kind voice stay with you, like a hand on your back, as you drift. [pause 30]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
We will end here for tonight. [pause 10]

Keep the feeling, not the effort. Let the effort go. [pause 15]

Whatever happens tomorrow, tonight you practiced feeling at peace. That is worth something on its own. [pause 20]

Let sleep come when it comes. There is no rush. [pause 20]

Notice the weight of the covers. The cool side of the pillow. The dark. [pause 25]

Let each breath out be a little longer than the one before. [pause 25]

Nothing more to picture. Nothing more to try. Only rest. [pause 30]

Good night. [pause 60]

pastor.note: Our own words only, no teacher named or quoted, no faith words; each teaching says it is imagination and feeling, not a promise, and keeps the daytime work real. Self-worth night gives 988 for thoughts of self-harm; old-memory revision tells listeners not to use abuse or trauma memories and to seek a trained person; evening walk makes no health or body promise and offers a non-walking version; family night never pictures forcing anyone to change; business night pictures ordinary enough, not riches, and says to get good advice.

cultural.note: Ordinary, dignified scenes (a family table, a bench on a trip, an open sign, a mirror) with no wealth or status fantasy; grandparents' hometown and family wounds named gently; pacing by silence (18.9-19.1 min).
